    95	
    96	2. **Flash/Turbo Variants Outpace Flagship Models**: Step 3.5 Flash, GLM 5 Turbo, Gemini 3 Flash, and other "fast and affordable" models see far higher usage than their flagship counterparts.      3	description: >
     4	  AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents
     5	  (PDF/DOCX/URL/Markdown) into high-quality SVG pages and exports to PPTX through

     8	---
     9	
    10	# PPT Master Skill
    11	
    12	> AI-driven multi-format SVG content generation system. Converts source documents into high-quality SVG pages through multi-role collaboration and exports to PPTX.
    13	
    14	**Core Pipeline**: `Source Document → Create Project → Template Option → Strategist → [Image_Generator] → Executor → Post-processing → Export`
    15	
    16	> [!CAUTION]
    17	> ## 🚨 Global Execution Discipline (MANDATORY)
    18	>
    19	> **This workflow is a strict serial pipeline. The following rules have the highest priority — violating any one of them constitutes execution failure:**
    20	>
    21	> 1. **SERIAL EXECUTION** — Steps MUST be executed in order; the output of each step is the input for the next. Non-BLOCKING adjacent steps may proceed continuously once prerequisites are met, without waiting for the user to say "continue"
    22	> 2. **BLOCKING = CONFIRMATION POINT** — Steps marked ⛔ BLOCKING are confirmation checkpoints. If a user is present, pause and wait for confirmation. If no user is available (e.g. automated / non-interactive mode), the AI should make professional recommendations based on the source material and proceed automatically
    23	> 3. **NO CROSS-PHASE BUNDLING** — Cross-phase bundling is FORBIDDEN. (Note: the Eight Confirmations in Step 4 are ⛔ BLOCKING — the AI should present recommendations and seek user confirmation when possible. Once confirmed (or auto-decided in non-interactive mode), all subsequent non-BLOCKING steps — design spec output, SVG generation, speaker notes, and post-processing — may proceed automatically without further confirmation)
    24	> 4. **GATE BEFORE ENTRY** — Each Step has prerequisites (🚧 GATE) listed at the top; these MUST be verified before starting that Step
    25	> 5. **NO SPECULATIVE EXECUTION** — "Pre-preparing" content for subsequent Steps is FORBIDDEN (e.g., writing SVG code during the Strategist phase)
    26	> 6. **NO SUB-AGENT SVG GENERATION** — Executor Step 6 SVG generation is context-dependent and MUST be completed by the current main agent end-to-end. Delegating page SVG generation to sub-agents is FORBIDDEN
    27	> 7. **SEQUENTIAL PAGE GENERATION ONLY** — In Executor Step 6, after the global design context is confirmed, SVG pages MUST be generated sequentially page by page in one continuous pass. Grouped page batches (for example, 5 pages at a time) are FORBIDDEN
    28	
    29	> [!IMPORTANT]
    30	> ## 🌐 Language & Communication Rule
    31	>
    32	> - **Response language**: Always match the language of the user's input and provided source materials. For example, if the user asks in Chinese, respond in Chinese; if the source material is in English, respond in English.
    33	> - **Explicit override**: If the user explicitly requests a specific language (e.g., "请用英文回答" or "Reply in Chinese"), use that language instead.
    34	> - **Template format**: The `design_spec.md` file MUST always follow its original English template structure (section headings, field names), regardless of the conversation language. Content values within the template may be in the user's language.
    35	
    36	> [!IMPORTANT]
    37	> ## 🔌 Compatibility With Generic Coding Skills
    38	>
    39	> - `ppt-master` is a repository-specific workflow skill, not a general application scaffold
    40	> - Do NOT create or require `.worktrees/`, `tests/`, branch workflows, or other generic engineering structure by default
    41	> - If another generic coding skill suggests repository conventions that conflict with this workflow, follow this skill first unless the user explicitly asks otherwise
    42	
    43	## Main Pipeline Scripts
    44	
    45	| Script | Purpose |
    46	|--------|---------|
    47	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/pdf_to_md.py` | PDF to Markdown |
    48	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py` | Documents to Markdown via Pandoc (DOCX, EPUB, HTML, LaTeX, RST, etc.) |
    49	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.py` | Web page to Markdown |
    50	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.cjs` | WeChat / high-security sites to Markdown |
    51	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/project_manager.py` | Project init / validate / manage |
    52	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/analyze_images.py` | Image analysis |
    53	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/image_gen.py` | AI image generation (multi-provider) |
    54	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/svg_quality_checker.py` | SVG quality check |
    55	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/total_md_split.py` | Speaker notes splitting |
    56	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/finalize_svg.py` | SVG post-processing (unified entry) |
    57	| `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/svg_to_pptx.py` | Export to PPTX |
    58	
    59	For complete tool documentation, see `${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/README.md`.

    63	| Index | Path | Purpose |

    77	## Workflow
    78	
    79	### Step 1: Source Content Processing
    80	
    81	🚧 **GATE**: User has provided source material (PDF / DOCX / EPUB / URL / Markdown file / text description / conversation content — any form is acceptable).
    82

    84	
    85	| User Provides | Command |
    86	|---------------|---------|
    87	| PDF file | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/pdf_to_md.py <file>` |
    88	| DOCX / Word / Office document | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py <file>` |
    89	| EPUB / HTML / LaTeX / RST / other | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/doc_to_md.py <file>` |
    90	| Web link | `python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.py <URL>` |
    91	| WeChat / high-security site | `node ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/web_to_md.cjs <URL>` |
    92	| Markdown | Read directly |

    97	
    98	### Step 2: Project Initialization
    99	
   100	🚧 **GATE**: Step 1 complete; source content is ready (Markdown file, user-provided text, or requirements described in conversation are all valid).
   101	
   102	```bash
   103	python3 ${SKILL_DIR}/scripts/project_manager.py init <project_name> --format <format>
   104	```
   105	
   106	Format options: `ppt169` (default), `ppt43`, `xhs`, `story`, etc. For the full format list, see `references/canvas-formats.md`.

   114	
   115	> ⚠️ **MUST use `--move`**: All source files (original PDF / MD / images) MUST be **moved** (not copied) into `sources/` for archiving.
   116	> - Markdown files generated in Step 1, original PDFs, original MDs — **all** must be moved into the project via `import-sources --move`
   117	> - Intermediate artifacts (e.g., `_files/` directories) are handled automatically by `import-sources`

   124	### Step 3: Template Selection
   125

   127	
   128	⛔ **BLOCKING**: If the user has not yet clearly expressed whether to use a template, present options and seek user input. If no user is available, choose the most appropriate template based on content topic and tone, or choose free-design. If the user has previously stated "no template" or specified a particular template, skip this prompt and proceed directly.

   131	Query `${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/layouts_index.json` to list available templates and their style descriptions.

   133	
   134	> 💡 **AI Recommendation**: Based on your content topic (brief summary), I recommend **[specific template / free design]** because...
   135	>
   136	> Which approach would you prefer?
   137	> **A) Use an existing template** (please specify template name or style preference)
   138	> **B) No template** — free design
   139	
   140	After the user confirms option A, copy template files to the project directory:
   141	```bash
   142	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/*.svg <project_path>/templates/
   143	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/design_spec.md <project_path>/templates/
   144	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/*.png <project_path>/images/ 2>/dev/null || true
   145	cp ${SKILL_DIR}/templates/layouts/<template_name>/*.jpg <project_path>/images/ 2>/dev/null || true
   146	```
   147	
   148	After the user confirms option B, proceed directly to Step 4.
   149	
   150	> To create a new global template, read `workflows/create-template.md`

   157	
   158	🚧 **GATE**: Step 3 complete; user has confirmed template selection.
   159

   162	Read references/strategist.md

If no user is available, apply professional defaults: read canvas/page-count/audience/style from the task input, and choose color/icon/typography/image settings based on content and tone.    182	
   183	> ⚠️ **Image handling rule**: The AI must NEVER directly read, open, or view image files (`.jpg`, `.png`, etc.). All image information must come from the `analyze_images.py` script output or the Design Specification's Image Resource List.

   197	### Step 5: Image_Generator Phase (Conditional)
   198

See executor-base.md Section 2 for details.

Do NOT delegate any slide SVG generation to sub-agents.

   239	
   240	**Visual Construction Phase**:
   241	- Generate SVG pages sequentially, one page at a time, in one continuous pass → `<project_path>/svg_output/`
   242	
   243	**Logic Construction Phase**:
   244	- Generate speaker notes → `<project_path>/notes/total.md`

   255	### Step 7: Post-processing & Export

   257	🚧 **GATE**: Step 6 complete; all SVGs generated to `svg_output/`; speaker notes `notes/total.md` generated.

   259	> ⚠️ The following three sub-steps MUST be **executed individually one at a time**. Each command must complete and be confirmed successful before running the next.

   261	
   262	**Step 7.1** — Split speaker notes:

     6	
     7	## 1. SVG Banned Features Blacklist
     8	
     9	The following features are **absolutely forbidden** when generating SVGs — PPT export will break if any are used:
    10	
    11	| Banned Feature | Description |
    12	|----------------|-------------|
    13	| `clipPath` | Clipping paths |
    14	| `mask` | Masks |
    15	| `<style>` | Embedded stylesheets |
    16	| `class` | CSS selector attributes (`id` inside `<defs>` is a legitimate reference and is NOT banned) |
    17	| External CSS | External stylesheet links |
    18	| `<foreignObject>` | Embedded external content |
    19	| `<symbol>` + `<use>` | Symbol reference reuse |
    20	| `textPath` | Text along a path |
    21	| `@font-face` | Custom font declarations |
    22	| `<animate*>` / `<set>` | SVG animations |
    23	| `<script>` / event attributes | Scripts and interactivity |
    24	| `marker` / `marker-end` | Line endpoint markers |
    25	| `<iframe>` | Embedded frames |
    26	
    27	---
    28	
    29	## 2. PPT Compatibility Alternatives
    30	
    31	| Banned Syntax | Correct Alternative |
    32	|---------------|---------------------|
    33	| `fill="rgba(255,255,255,0.1)"` | `fill="#FFFFFF" fill-opacity="0.1"` |
    34	| `<g opacity="0.2">...</g>` | Set `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity` on each child element individually |
    35	| `<image opacity="0.3"/>` | Overlay a `<rect fill="background-color" opacity="0.7"/>` mask layer after the image |
    36	| `marker-end` arrows | Draw triangle arrows with `<polygon>` |
    37	
    38	**Mnemonic**: PPT does not recognize rgba, group opacity, image opacity, or markers.

    70	## 4. Basic SVG Rules
    71	
    72	- **viewBox** must match the canvas dimensions (`width`/`height` must match `viewBox`)
    73	- **Background**: Use `<rect>` to define the page background color
    74	- **Line breaks**: Use `<tspan>` for manual line breaks; `<foreignObject>` is FORBIDDEN
    75	- **Fonts**: Use system fonts only (Microsoft YaHei, Arial, Calibri, etc.); `@font-face` is FORBIDDEN
    76	- **Styles**: Use inline styles only (`fill="..."` `font-size="..."`); `<style>` / `class` are FORBIDDEN (`id` inside `<defs>` is legitimate)
    77	- **Colors**: Use HEX values; for transparency use `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`
    78	- **Image references**: `<image href="../images/xxx.png" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>`
    79	- **Icon placeholders**: `<use data-icon="icon-name" x="" y="" width="48" height="48" fill="#HEX"/>` (auto-embedded during post-processing)

    83	## 5. Post-processing Pipeline (3 Steps)
    84	
    85	Must be executed in order — skipping or adding extra flags is FORBIDDEN:
    86	
    87	```bash
    88	# 1. Split speaker notes into per-page note files
    89	python3 scripts/total_md_split.py <project_path>
    90	
    91	# 2. SVG post-processing (icon embedding, image crop/embed, text flattening, rounded rect to path)
    92	python3 scripts/finalize_svg.py <project_path>
    93	
    94	# 3. Export PPTX (from svg_final/, embeds speaker notes by default)
    95	python3 scripts/svg_to_pptx.py <project_path> -s final

    99	**Prohibited**:
   100	- NEVER use `cp` as a substitute for `finalize_svg.py`
   101	- NEVER export directly from `svg_output/` — MUST export from `svg_final/` (use `-s final`)
   102	- NEVER add extra flags like `--only`
   103	
   104	**Re-run rule**: Any modification to `svg_output/` after post-processing has completed (including page revisions, additions, or deletions) requires re-running Steps 2 and 3. Step 1 only needs re-running if `notes/total.md` was also modified.

   107	
   108	## 6. Shadow & Overlay Techniques
   109	
   110	> `<mask>` elements and `<image opacity="...">` are banned. Always use stacked `<rect>` or gradient overlays instead (see §2).
   111	
   112	### Shadow
   113	
   114	#### Filter Soft Shadow — Recommended
   115	
   116	Best for: cards, floating panels, elevated elements. `svg_to_shapes.py` automatically converts `feGaussianBlur` + `feOffset` into native PPTX `<a:outerShdw>`.
   117	
   118	```xml
   119	<defs>
   120	  <filter id="softShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   121	    <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="8"/>
   122	    <feOffset dx="0" dy="4" result="offsetBlur"/>
   123	    <feFlood flood-color="#000000" flood-opacity="0.08" result="shadowColor"/>
   124	    <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   125	    <feMerge>
   126	      <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   127	      <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   128	    </feMerge>
   129	  </filter>
   130	</defs>
   131	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF" filter="url(#softShadow)"/>
   132	```
   133	
   134	Recommended parameters:
   135	```
   136	stdDeviation:   6–10     (smaller = crisper, larger = softer)
   137	flood-opacity:  0.06–0.12  (keep low for a premium feel)
   138	dy:             3–6      (vertical > horizontal for natural top-light)
   139	dx:             0–2
   140	```
   141	
   142	#### Colored Shadow
   143	
   144	Best for: accent buttons, brand-colored cards. Use the element's own color family instead of black.
   145	
   146	```xml
   147	<filter id="colorShadow" x="-15%" y="-15%" width="140%" height="140%">
   148	  <feGaussianBlur in="SourceAlpha" stdDeviation="10"/>
   149	  <feOffset dx="0" dy="6" result="offsetBlur"/>
   150	  <feFlood flood-color="#1A73E8" flood-opacity="0.20" result="shadowColor"/>
   151	  <feComposite in="shadowColor" in2="offsetBlur" operator="in" result="shadow"/>
   152	  <feMerge>
   153	    <feMergeNode in="shadow"/>
   154	    <feMergeNode in="SourceGraphic"/>
   155	  </feMerge>
   156	</filter>
   157	```
   158	
   159	Replace `flood-color` with the element's brand color; keep `flood-opacity` between 0.12–0.20.
   160	
   161	#### Layered Rect Shadow — High-Compatibility Fallback
   162	
   163	Best for: maximum compatibility with older PowerPoint versions. Stack 2–3 semi-transparent rectangles behind the main card:
   164	
   165	```xml
   166	<!-- Shadow layers (back to front, largest offset first) -->
   167	<rect x="68" y="72" width="400" height="240" rx="16" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.03"/>
   168	<rect x="65" y="69" width="400" height="240" rx="14" fill="#000000" fill-opacity="0.05"/>
   169	<rect x="62" y="66" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#1A73E8" fill-opacity="0.04"/>
   170	<!-- Main card -->
   171	<rect x="60" y="60" width="400" height="240" rx="12" fill="#FFFFFF"/>
   172	```
   173	
   174	### Image Overlay
   175	
   176	#### Linear Gradient Overlay — Most Common
   177	
   178	Best for: image+text pages. Gradient direction should match text position (text on left → gradient darkens toward left).
   179	
   180	```xml
   181	<image href="..." x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice"/>
   182	<defs>
   183	  <linearGradient id="imgOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   184	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.85"/>
   185	    <stop offset="55%"  stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0.30"/>
   186	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#1A1A2E" stop-opacity="0"/>
   187	  </linearGradient>
   188	</defs>
   189	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#imgOverlay)"/>
   190	```
   191	
   192	#### Bottom Gradient Bar
   193	
   194	Best for: cover slides and full-image pages with bottom title.
   195	
   196	```xml
   197	<defs>
   198	  <linearGradient id="bottomBar" x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
   199	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   200	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.72"/>
   201	  </linearGradient>
   202	</defs>
   203	<rect x="0" y="380" width="1280" height="340" fill="url(#bottomBar)"/>
   204	```
   205	
   206	#### Radial Gradient Overlay — Vignette Effect
   207	
   208	Best for: full-screen atmosphere slides; draws attention to the center.
   209	
   210	```xml
   211	<defs>
   212	  <radialGradient id="vignette" cx="50%" cy="50%" r="70%">
   213	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0"/>
   214	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#000000" stop-opacity="0.58"/>
   215	  </radialGradient>
   216	</defs>
   217	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#vignette)"/>
   218	```
   219	
   220	#### Brand Color Overlay
   221	
   222	Best for: slides needing strong visual brand identity.
   223	
   224	```xml
   225	<defs>
   226	  <linearGradient id="brandOverlay" x1="0" y1="0" x2="1" y2="0">
   227	    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.80"/>
   228	    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.10"/>
   229	  </linearGradient>
   230	</defs>
   231	<rect x="0" y="0" width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#brandOverlay)"/>
   232	```
   233	
   234	### Quick-Reference Table
   235	
   236	| Scenario | Recommended Technique | Avoid |
   237	|----------|-----------------------|-------|
   238	| Card / panel shadow | Filter soft shadow (`flood-opacity` ≤ 0.12) | Hard black shadow |
   239	| Accent / CTA button | Colored shadow (same hue family) | Generic gray shadow |
   240	| Text over image | Linear gradient overlay (direction matches text side) | Uniform flat opacity over whole image |
   241	| Cover / full-image slide | Bottom gradient bar + brand color | Solid black overlay |
   242	| Atmosphere / hero slide | Radial vignette | Unprocessed raw image |
   243	| Max PPT compatibility needed | Layered rect shadow | Filter-based shadow |

     5	---
     6	
     7	## Role Definition
     8	
     9	A data-driven, consulting-style SVG design executor. Suitable for business analysis reports, market research, operational reviews, strategic recommendations, and other **general consulting** scenarios. Emphasizes structured information presentation and data visualization; clean, clear, and professional style.
    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	## Consultant-specific Data Visualization Techniques
    14	
    15	### 1. KPI Dashboard Design
    16	
    17	KPI cards are the most common element in consulting reports. Standard layout (1280x720):
    18	
    19	```
    20	4-card layout: each card 280x180, gap 30
    21	  Card 1: x=45,  y=160
    22	  Card 2: x=355, y=160
    23	  Card 3: x=665, y=160
    24	  Card 4: x=975, y=160
    25	```
    26	
    27	**Card internal structure** (top to bottom):
    28	
    29	| Area | Content | Font Size | Style |
    30	|------|---------|-----------|-------|
    31	| Icon row | data-icon icon | 32x32 | Theme color |
    32	| Metric name | "Monthly Active Users" | 14px | Gray #64748B |
    33	| Core number | "1.2M" | 36-42px | Bold, dark color |
    34	| Trend annotation | "+12.3% vs last month" | 12px | Green=up / Red=down |
    35	
    36	**Trend arrow conventions**:
    37	- Up: `arrow-trend-up` icon + green text
    38	- Down: `arrow-trend-down` icon + red text
    39	- Flat: horizontal line icon + gray text
    40	
    41	### 2. Chart Color Conventions
    42	
    43	Consulting-style charts use **monochromatic depth gradients** rather than rainbow colors:
    44	
    45	```
    46	Primary series:   Theme color 100% opacity
    47	Comparison series: Theme color 60% opacity
    48	Baseline:         #94A3B8 (gray dashed line)
    49	Highlight:        Accent color (only for key data points)
    50	```
    51	
    52	### 3. Data Annotation Principles
    53	
    54	- **Direct data labels**: Place values at the top of bar charts — no legend needed
    55	- **Annotated trend lines**: Add text notes at key inflection points ("Policy change", "Product launch")
    56	- **Comparison baselines**: Mark industry average / target values with gray dashed lines
    57	- **Consistent units**: Maintain the same numeric units and precision within a chart
    58	
    59	### 4. Table Design
    60	
    61	Consulting reports frequently use tables for precise data:
    62	
    63	| Design Element | Specification |
    64	|----------------|---------------|
    65	| Header | Dark background + white text, font-weight="bold" |
    66	| Zebra striping | Alternate rows with `fill-opacity="0.05"` light background |
    67	| Number alignment | Numbers right-aligned, text left-aligned |
    68	| Highlighted row | Mark key rows with accent color `fill-opacity="0.1"` |
    69	| Borders | Use horizontal lines only to separate rows; avoid full grid lines |
    70	
    71	---
    72	
    73	## Consulting-specific Layout Patterns
    74	
    75	### MECE Decomposition Tree
    76	
    77	Main trunk on the left, branches expanding rightward — mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive:
    78	
    79	```
    80	Main metric ──┬── Branch A (45%)
    81	              ├── Branch B (30%)
    82	              ├── Branch C (20%)
    83	              └── Branch D (5%)
    84	```
    85	
    86	- Use `<line>` to connect trunk to branches
    87	- Each branch has a `<rect>` container + percentage annotation
    88	- Sum must = 100% (or explicitly label "Other")
    89	
    90	### Driver Factor Tree
    91	
    92	Top-level metric → decomposed factors → actions. Ideal for performance attribution analysis:
    93	
    94	```
    95	Revenue growth 15%
    96	  ├── Average order value +8%  → Premium product line expansion
    97	  ├── Customer count +5%       → New channel acquisition
    98	  └── Repurchase rate +2%      → Loyalty program optimization
    99	```
   100	
   101	### Left-chart Right-text (Chart Interpretation)
   102	
   103	Core consulting report layout: chart on the left, key insights on the right:
   104	
   105	```
   106	Chart area: x=40, y=120, w=700, h=480
   107	Insight area: x=780, y=120, w=460, h=480
   108	  - Core conclusion (bold, 16px)
   109	  - 3-5 bullet points (14px)
   110	  - Data source (12px, gray)
   111	```
   112	
   113	---
   114	
   115	## Professional Expression Standards
   116	
   117	### Page Titles
   118	
   119	Consulting-style page titles should be **assertion headlines**, not descriptive titles:
   120	
   121	| Type | Descriptive (avoid) | Assertion (recommended) |
   122	|------|---------------------|------------------------|
   123	| Market | "Market Overview" | "Domestic market grows 23% YoY, significantly outpacing global average" |
   124	| Competition | "Competitive Analysis" | "Three major competitors show clear weaknesses in channel coverage" |
   125	| Finance | "Financial Data" | "Gross margin improved for four consecutive quarters, breaking industry ceiling" |
   126	
   127	### Data Source Attribution
   128	
   129	Every data-containing page must include a source note at the bottom:
   130	
   131	```xml
   132	<text x="40" y="700" font-size="10" fill="#94A3B8">
   133	  Source: National Bureau of Statistics 2025 Annual Report; Internal team analysis
   134	</text>
   135	```
   136	
   137	### Key Takeaway Box
   138	
   139	Consulting-style content pages should include a **Takeaway Box** below the title:
   140	
   141	```
   142	Position: x=40, y=80, w=1200, h=50
   143	Background: Light theme color (fill-opacity="0.08")
   144	Text: 14-16px, one-sentence summary of the page's core takeaway
   145	```
   146	
   147	---
   148	
   149	## Speaker Notes Style
   150	
   151	### Narrative Tone
   152	
   153	Consultant-style speaker notes use a **conclusion-driven** approach — state the conclusion first, then present supporting evidence. Professional, concise, and persuasive tone.
   154	
   155	### Stage Direction Markers
   156	
   157	| Marker | Purpose | Example |
   158	|--------|---------|---------|
   159	| `[Pause]` | Silence after key conclusions, let the audience absorb | "This means our market share is being eroded. [Pause]" |
   160	| `[Data]` | Cue to verbalize numbers conversationally | "[Data] 85% → more than eight out of ten customers reported this issue" |
   161	| `[Transition]` | Bridge from previous page, must be at start of each page's text | "[Transition] Based on that analysis, let's look at specific recommendations." |
   162	
   163	### Notes Writing Guidelines
   164	
   165	- **Conclusion first**: The first sentence of each page's notes is the core takeaway
   166	- **Conversational data**: 30% → "roughly one-third", 85% → "more than eight out of ten", 2.5x → "two and a half times"
   167	- **Evidence follows immediately**: After the conclusion, provide 2-3 supporting data points/facts
   168	- **Professional terminology**: Use terms like "insight", "driver", "key lever" etc.
   169	- **Key points structure**: `Key points: (1) Core conclusion (2) Supporting data (3) Next steps`
   170	
   171	### Notes Example
   172	
   173	```markdown
   174	# 03_key_findings
   175	
   176	[Transition] Based on our market scan, we have distilled three key findings.
   177	
   178	First, the primary growth driver is shifting from acquisition to retention.
   179	[Data] New customer acquisition cost rose nearly 40% year-over-year, yet improved repurchase rates contributed over 60% of revenue growth. [Pause]
   180	
   181	Second, lower-tier market growth significantly outpaces tier-1 and tier-2 cities.
   182	Third, the 25-35 female user segment has an ARPU 1.8x the overall average.
   183	
   184	Key points: (1) Growth engine shifting from acquisition to retention (2) Lower-tier market opportunity window (3) High-value user persona
   185	Duration: 2 minutes
   186	```
   187	
   188	---
   189	
   190	## Self-check Supplement (Consultant-specific)
   191	
   192	- [ ] Data matches source data — no fabrication
   193	- [ ] Every data page has a source attribution at the bottom
   194	- [ ] Page titles are assertion-based, not descriptive
   195	- [ ] KPI cards have trend arrows and comparison annotations
   196	- [ ] Chart colors are unified, using monochromatic scheme rather than rainbow
   197	- [ ] Notes are conclusion-first with conversational data

# OpenRouter LLM Report - Design Spec

## I. Project Information

| Item | Value |
| ---- | ----- |
| **Project Name** | openrouter_llm_report |
| **Canvas Format** | PPT 16:9 (1280×720) |
| **Page Count** | 7 |
| **Design Style** | General Consulting (McKinsey template) |
| **Target Audience** | LLM industry professionals (R&D, product, investment) |
| **Use Case** | Data-driven market analysis report on LLM usage landscape |
| **Created Date** | 2026-04-27 |

---

## II. Canvas Specification

| Property | Value |
| -------- | ----- |
| **Format** | PPT 16:9 |
| **Dimensions** | 1280×720 |
| **viewBox** | `0 0 1280 720` |
| **Margins** | Left/right 60px, top 80px (header), bottom 80px (footer) |
| **Content Area** | x=60, y=170, width=1160, height=450 |

---

## III. Visual Theme

### Theme Style

- **Style**: General Consulting (B)
- **Theme**: Light theme (white background + McKinsey blue accent)
- **Tone**: Data-forward, engaging, professional — authoritative yet accessible for technical audiences

### Color Scheme

| Role | HEX | Purpose |
| ---- | --- | ------- |
| **Background** | `#FFFFFF` | Page background |
| **Secondary bg** | `#FAFBFC` | Header/footer background, card backgrounds |
| **Primary** | `#005587` | Title decorations, key sections, icons, header bars |
| **Accent** | `#F5A623` | Data highlights, key information, insight bars, positive indicators |
| **Secondary accent** | `#0076A8` | Gradient transitions, secondary emphasis |
| **Body text** | `#2C3E50` | Main body text |
| **Secondary text** | `#5D6D7E` | Subtitles, captions |
| **Tertiary text** | `#7F8C8D` | Footers, annotations, source notes |
| **Border/divider** | `#E5E7EB` | Card borders, divider lines |
| **Success** | `#2E7D32` | Positive growth indicators |
| **Warning** | `#E74C3C` | Negative trends, decline indicators |

### Gradient Scheme

```xml
<!-- Header gradient -->
<linearGradient id="headerGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="0%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#005587"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#0076A8"/>
</linearGradient>

<!-- Decorative gradient -->
<linearGradient id="decoGrad" x1="0%" y1="0%" x2="100%" y2="100%">
  <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#005587" stop-opacity="0.12"/>
  <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#0076A8" stop-opacity="0.04"/>
</linearGradient>
```

---

## IV. Typography System

### Font Plan

**Recommended preset**: P5 (English-primary)

| Role | Chinese | English | Fallback |
| ---- | ------- | ------- | -------- |
| **Title** | Microsoft YaHei | Arial | sans-serif |
| **Body** | Microsoft YaHei | Calibri | Arial, sans-serif |
| **Code** | - | Consolas | Monaco |
| **Emphasis** | SimHei | Arial Black | sans-serif |

**Font stack**: `Arial, Calibri, sans-serif`

### Font Size Hierarchy

**Baseline**: Body font size = 18px (dense data content)

| Purpose | Ratio | 18px baseline | Weight |
| ------- | ----- | ------------- | ------ |
| Cover title | 3x | 54px | Bold |
| Content title | 1.8x | 32px | Bold |
| Subtitle | 1.3x | 24px | SemiBold |
| **Body content** | **1x** | **18px** | Regular |
| Annotation | 0.75x | 14px | Regular |
| Page number/date | 0.6x | 11px | Regular |

---

## V. Layout Principles

### Page Structure

- **Header area**: y=0 to y=80 (top gradient bar + page title + section label)
- **Content area**: y=170 to y=620 (width 1160px, height 450px)
- **Footer area**: y=640 to y=720 (source notes, page number)

### Common Layout Modes

| Mode | Suitable Scenarios |
| ---- | ----------------- |
| **Single column centered** | Cover, ending |
| **Left-right split (5:5)** | Chart + insight text (slides 2, 3, 5, 6) |
| **Top-bottom split** | KPI cards + details |
| **Matrix grid (2×2)** | Takeaways, trend observations |

### Spacing Specification

| Element | Recommended Range | Current Project |
| ------- | ---------------- | --------------- |
| Card gap | 20-32px | 24px |
| Content block gap | 24-40px | 32px |
| Card padding | 20-32px | 20px |
| Card border radius | 8-16px | 6px |
| Icon-text gap | 8-16px | 12px |
| Single-row card height | 530-600px | — |
| Double-row card height | 265-295px each | — |
| Three-column card width | 360-380px each | 370px |

---

## VI. Icon Usage Specification

### Source

- **Built-in icon library**: `templates/icons/` (640+ icons)
- **Usage method**: Placeholder format `<use data-icon="icon-name" .../>`

### Recommended Icon List

| Purpose | Icon Name | Page |
| ------- | --------- | ---- |
| Data/chart | `chart-bar` | Slide 2, 3 |
| Growth trend | `arrow-trend-up` | Slide 5 |
| Market share | `chart-pie` | Slide 3 |
| Users/apps | `users` | Slide 6 |
| Lightbulb insight | `lightbulb` | Slide 7 |
| Checkmark | `circle-checkmark` | Slide 7 |
| Rocket | `rocket` | Slide 5 |
| Globe | `globe` | Slide 4 |
| Code | `code` | Slide 6 |
| Target | `target` | Slide 4 |
| Database | `database` | Slide 1 |
| Trophy | `trophy` | Slide 2 |

---

## VII. Chart Reference List

| Chart Type | Reference Template | Used In |
| ---------- | ------------------ | ------- |
| horizontal_bar_chart | `templates/charts/horizontal_bar_chart.svg` | Slide 02 (Top 10 Models ranking) |
| pie_chart | `templates/charts/pie_chart.svg` | Slide 03 (Provider Market Share) |

---

## VIII. Image Resource List

No images required. This is a data-driven consulting report; all visuals are charts, tables, and data cards.

---

## IX. Content Outline

### Part 1: Market Overview

#### Slide 01 - Cover

- **Layout**: Full-screen (template `01_cover.svg`)
- **Title**: The 2025 LLM Usage Landscape: Real-World Data from OpenRouter
- **Subtitle**: Based on real usage data from millions of OpenRouter users — over 26T tokens processed this week
- **Info**: OpenRouter Rankings | March 2025

#### Slide 02 - This Week's Top 10 Models

- **Layout**: Left-right split (chart left, insights right)
- **Title**: This Week's Top 10 Models
- **Chart**: horizontal_bar_chart (ranking by weekly token usage)
- **Content**:
  - Table/bar chart showing Rank, Model, Provider, Weekly Token Usage, WoW Change
  - MiMo-V2-Pro (Xiaomi) leads at 3.96T tokens, +165% WoW
  - Chinese providers hold 6 of top 10 spots
  - MiniMax M2.7 strongest growth at +253%
  - Anthropic's two models combine for ~2T but growth stalled

#### Slide 03 - Provider Market Share Breakdown

- **Layout**: Left-right split (pie chart left, insights right)
- **Title**: Provider Market Share Breakdown
- **Chart**: pie_chart (token share by provider)
- **Content**:
  - Xiaomi 25.9%, Google 11.8%, Anthropic 11.0%, MiniMax 8.5%, OpenAI 7.9%
  - Combined Chinese provider share ≈ 54.3% (exceeds half the market)
  - OpenAI ranks only fifth at 7.9%
  - Market is highly fragmented — no provider exceeds 30%
  - Note: provider-level share includes all models/apps, not just top 10

#### Slide 04 - Shifts in the Market Landscape

- **Layout**: 2×2 matrix grid (4 trend observations)
- **Title**: Shifts in the Market Landscape
- **Content**:
  - Chinese models break through globally: 54%+ share on international platform
  - Flash/Turbo variants outpace flagship models: users prioritize speed & cost
  - AI coding agents dominate usage: largest commercial value proposition
  - Highly fragmented market: top 10 spans 8 providers, competition fierce
  - Reference: weekly token usage grew from ~2T to ~26T

#### Slide 05 - This Week's Rising Stars: Fastest-Growing Models

- **Layout**: Top KPI cards + bottom detail list
- **Title**: This Week's Rising Stars: Fastest-Growing Models
- **Content**:
  - MiniMax M2.7: +253% (MiniMax)
  - MiMo-V2-Pro: +165% (Xiaomi)
  - Cline (coding agent): +128% (Independent developer)
  - Hermes Agent: +92% (Nous Research)
  - Ampere: +576% (Ampere)
  - Codex: +112% (OpenAI)
  - Drivers: cost-performance advantage, coding agent demand, flash model preference

#### Slide 06 - App Ecosystem: Who's Calling These Models

- **Layout**: Left-right split (table left, insight right)
- **Title**: App Ecosystem: Who's Calling These Models
- **Content**:
  - Top apps by daily token consumption table
  - OpenClaw: 829B tokens/day (nearly 3× second place)
  - Kilo Code: 271B, Claude Code: 78B, Cline: 69.1B
  - Top 4 apps are all AI coding tools
  - AI coding agents = single largest LLM consumption scenario
  - Entertainment apps (Janitor AI, ISEKAI ZERO) still notable

#### Slide 07 - Key Insights and Industry Implications

- **Layout**: 2×2 takeaway cards + bottom summary bar
- **Title**: Key Insights and Industry Implications
- **Content**:
  - Chinese models now hold dominant share in global market (54%+)
  - AI coding agents are the single largest LLM consumption scenario
  - Model market is highly fragmented with no outright winner
  - Affordable/fast models (Flash/Turbo) far outpace flagship models in usage
  - The landscape is far from settled — competition remains fierce

---

## X. Speaker Notes Requirements

- **File naming**: Match SVG names, e.g., `01_cover.md`, `02_top_models.md`
- **Content includes**: Script key points, timing cues, transition phrases
- **Style**: Professional, conclusion-first, data-driven
- **Duration estimate**: 15-20 minutes total (2-3 min per slide)

---

## XI. Technical Constraints Reminder

### SVG Generation Must Follow:

1. viewBox: `0 0 1280 720`
2. Background uses `<rect>` elements
3. Text wrapping uses `<tspan>` (`<foreignObject>` FORBIDDEN)
4. Transparency uses `fill-opacity` / `stroke-opacity`; `rgba()` FORBIDDEN
5. FORBIDDEN: `clipPath`, `mask`, `<style>`, `class`, `foreignObject`
6. FORBIDDEN: `textPath`, `animate*`, `script`, `marker`/`marker-end`
7. Arrows use `<polygon>` triangles instead of `<marker>`

### PPT Compatibility Rules:

- `<g opacity="...">` FORBIDDEN (group opacity); set on each child element individually
- Image transparency uses overlay mask layer
- Inline styles only; external CSS and `@font-face` FORBIDDEN

---

## XII. Design Checklist

### Pre-generation

- [ ] Content fits page capacity
- [ ] Layout mode selected correctly
- [ ] Colors used semantically

### Post-generation

- [ ] viewBox = `0 0 1280 720`
- [ ] No `<foreignObject>` elements
- [ ] All text readable (>=14px)
- [ ] Content within safe area
- [ ] All elements aligned to grid
- [ ] Same elements maintain consistent style
- [ ] Colors conform to spec
- [ ] CRAP four-principle check passed

Perhaps most surprising to Western audiences: OpenAI ranks only fifth at 7.9%. The market is also highly fragmented — no single provider exceeds 30%, and the top 10 spans 8 different providers. [Pause]

[Transition] These numbers reveal four major shifts reshaping the competitive landscape.

First, Chinese models have broken through globally. On an international platform, Chinese providers now account for over half of all usage — Xiaomi's MiMo series, DeepSeek V3, and MiniMax's M2 series hold a significant cost-performance advantage.

Second, Flash and Turbo variants are outpacing flagship models. Step 3.5 Flash, GLM 5 Turbo, Gemini 3 Flash — these "fast and affordable" models see far higher usage than their flagship counterparts. Users are voting with their feet: in real-world applications, speed and cost often matter more than peak performance.

Third, AI coding agents dominate usage. Five of the top 10 apps are coding tools, reflecting the largest commercial value proposition for LLMs today.

Fourth, the market remains highly fragmented — no single model or provider monopolizes, signaling fierce competition and an unsettled landscape. [Pause]
